notes: No more glow around the hero at higher ranks: you look the same at every rank, and your gear is what shows. The rank-up moment stays, a burst of your class's light
The hero no longer grows a little with each rank
The camera sits a step further back: everyone is smaller on screen and you see more of the world
The save screen fits again with every slot full: long names and places wrap inside their cards, so the right-hand column is never cut off
The skills screen fits on narrow and tall screens too
The ways between maps are natural passes now: the cliffs part and the road runs through, with no signposts, no name boxes and no framed caves or torches
The roads to the Mirefen and the Deepwood run out through the ridge instead of into a cave
Entering a place, or walking into one of the Ashenreach's regions, shows its name once on a title card
Liane's observatory and Greyhold's keep open into rooms now, not straight into a cave: Liane's room with her desk and books, and Captain Hale's hall with his table, banners and armour
A stairwell in each room goes down to the cave, and going into the dark is a choice: the stair asks first
Coming back up from the Ice Cave or the cellars brings you into the room, beside the stair
Maren no longer skips a story: if you went far before visiting her, she tells each one in turn, oldest first, and the main quest's step that waits on it is met
The story says what really happened: five of the village climbed to mend the seal and only one came home, the dream counts three torches, and Fafnyr is awake on his hoard
Tam's Ladle, Captain Hale and Maren's lines now agree with where things were found, and the credits end: Thank you for staying.
The map shows the world as it stands: every map you've found is a page, turned with left and right, its roads out and regions named, and the village drawn small inside its walls
Seven new waypoints reach every region: Saltmere Hamlet, the Sea Cave, the Miners' Camp, Gunnar's Camp, Liane's Observatory, the Old Guard's Camp and the Keep Yard
The waypoint list shows every waypoint under its place, greys the ones not found yet, and names the region where you land
The chosen waypoint's ring and its marker share one centre at any window size
The line under the title now says what the game is about: The village burned. You stayed.
Every way out of a map reads as a way on: the road runs right to it, through an opening wide enough to look walkable, and a signpost names where it leads
Cave mouths are framed and lit by torches, the mountain gate stands in the rock, and stairs up name the place above
New roads lead across the Ashenreach to the Mirefen and Deepwood passes and to the Undermountain, and a path climbs to Saltmere's sea cave
A way out on a map's south edge no longer hides under the dock, and you arrive facing into the new map, on its road
The quest marks over villagers sit centred on their heads, whichever way they face, and hold still while they breathe or walk
A monster's alert and fright bubbles sit centred over its head, and a named monster's plate over its health bar
Damage numbers and the spoils that float up are centred on the foe, on whole pixels
Reaching a new rank is a moment: the world darkens, a shaft of your class's light lifts the hero, the old look burns away into the new, and the rank's name and what it unlocks follow
Each rank shows on the hero, in the class's colours: an edge at rank II, a rim of light at III, a weapon that glows as it strikes at IV, and light trailing your steps at V
The rank's look sits over your clothes and gear and never hides them; with Reduce motion the old look simply fades into the new

Monsters keep hours: after dark, night packs come out in every region under the sky, wolves and skeletons in the forest, ghosts over the marsh, shades in the Deepwood, wendigos on the Frostgate Pass, a little stronger and richer than by day
Some day camps sleep by their lit torch at night, a Z drifting up: walk right up to one or strike it and the whole pack wakes
Packs change at dusk and dawn only out of your sight, and every quest's quarry can be found at any hour
Where a monster is found only after dark, the places it lives say so

The title screen comes alive: a slow camera drifts over the street under the mountain, the torches, the lit windows and the watchman's lantern pool warm light on the walls and the road, and the moon and the flames glow
A lake behind the square swells and glints, the trees and the hill's pines lean in the wind, mist rolls along the valley and embers rise off the torches
With Reduce motion the scene holds still, and the world behind the title rests, so the title costs no more to draw than before

XP, gold and loot float up from where you won them, the fallen foe, the chest, the patch or the water, like the damage numbers: XP in sea-glass green, gold behind a coin, each item with its icon in its rarity's colour
Quick wins stack: a pack's kills rise as one float that counts up, not a pile of lines
The log keeps only what the world doesn't show: the story, quests, levels, mastery, bounties and the Boss Slayer's edge
With Reduce motion, the wins fade in where they stand
On the town's tour, a rebuilt building rises at its stop: the ruin gives way in a cloud of dust, the walls go up row by row, and it lands under confetti
Under its name, what it brings: who is back at work, the new perk, or who has moved into town
The tour now looks at the inn itself and at the flower beds, and its dust drifts instead of hanging in the air
With Reduce motion, the ruin stands a moment and then the building is there
The hero walks in four beats, rising as the feet pass, each step timed to the ground it covers, so the feet no longer slide
Villagers, monsters and the wagon step at their own pace too, keep their stride through a turn and settle a moment when they stop
Wolves, spiders, cats, the mammoths and many villagers no longer walk backwards when they go left or right
Villagers keep looking the way they walked a moment before turning back to the street, and the King Slime hops all the way up

The village seen from outside is the village you walk in: its own houses and roofs, the river with its bridge, its fields and woods, inside one ring of its rampart, the road running in through the gate
At night its windows and lamps are lit, and smoke rises from its roofs
It grows as you rebuild it, from the Town Hall alone among the ashes to the city's lamps and fountain
What grows on the ground moves from day to day: each morning a region grows its few patches in new spots, on bare ground away from villages, camps and roads
Each material grows a set number a day, so the rare ones stay rare: one Frost Lily, one Blackiron Ore and one Old Steel a day, their two homes taking turns
A dungeon floor's patch grows once a day, somewhere new in its first hall
Monsters far below your level run when they see you: a pale exclamation mark, a bead of sweat and a yelp. Corner one or strike it and it fights back; bosses and named monsters never run
A monster running from you doesn't start the battle music
The exclamation mark over a monster that has seen you sits above its level, which no longer hides its dot

The journal opens on what you're doing now: the quest you follow, its step, where to go and how far along you are. Under it, every open thread in one list, the main story, the town's quests and the board's bounties, each with its next step and its place

Choose a row with the arrows, the pad or the mouse and follow it with E, the pad's A or a click: the line over the dock, the arrow and the map's goal turn to it at once. A bounty you follow leads to its quarry's lair
Liane's pages and the feats are the journal's two other tabs, where there were five chapters
Where regions meet, the ground no longer changes along straight lines and square corners: the edge bends and wanders, still dithered pixel by pixel, and the land's tone runs right to the shore
The arrow toward your goal keeps clear of the line over the dock
The map screen reads cleanly: its legend sits under the map, the HUD steps aside while it's open, and keys like the comma show as their mark instead of their name

Every hero starts as a survivor of the Night of Ash: plain worker's clothes in the colour you chose, whatever the role; hero creation still shows the role's full kit, what you'll become, and gear shows on you as you put it on
A day lasts three times longer, and a clock at the top right tells the hour: a sun by day, a moon by night

Sleep till morning: face a bed at the inn (for the night's coin) or your own bed at home and press E; the screen goes dark and you wake at dawn, restored. Walking into the inn no longer takes a bed by itself
Rent and the bank's interest still come by the day, so with longer days they come in less often
The line above the dock says where: the next step, the place it's in and how far along you are
A gold arrow at the edge of the screen points the way while your goal is out of sight, to the person, the spot or the door that leads there; the map marks it with a gold diamond

Hero creation reads clearly: the first night is a setting of its own (The first night (tutorial): Play / Skip, with a line on what each means), and Begin the adventure is the start, alone at the bottom; Tab, a click or the pad's Y flips the night, and a pad can now reach every control

Fast travel shows where it takes you: the waypoint you choose on the map gets a gold ring, its name and the region you'll land in, and the map turns to that place; choose with the arrows, the pad or the mouse
A gold ! over someone with a quest for you, a gold ? over someone waiting for you to hand one in, and a grey ? while a quest you took from them is under way; Options can turn them off (Quest markers)
Fixed: no more black squares around the smithy's forges or the hearths of the inn and your house; they stand against the wall now, and in the bigger houses the oven moves so both beds can be slept in
Fixed: the Mirefen's bridges cross the river instead of running along it or standing alone in a pond, its maze chest can be reached, and the town's bridge and dock sit right in the water
Face a forge, an anvil or a cauldron and press E to craft there; the inn's hearth tells you where the stew is brewed, and a recipe you can't make yet says what it still needs
Fixed: after funding a project on the square, the town's tour of what was built played behind a black screen; it shows in full now, and so do the ending's tour and the homecomings
Fixed: skill points no longer pile up with nothing to buy; the skill tree's last tiers now open at levels 9, 11 and 14 instead of 10, 13 and 17
Named monsters like Rimefang now fall as bosses do: the world slows, the music cuts, and a Victory title marks it
Bosses and named monsters no longer give up the chase and heal when you step away, and there's no leaving while one hunts you
Slaying one makes you a Boss slayer: +10% damage for 10 minutes, counting down at the top left
Fixed: a potion you brewed before taking Vex's "A First Brew" now counts as soon as you take it, and whatever you craft for a quest you've taken says in the battle log when it's ready to hand in
The camera no longer leans ahead of your hero: it made them slip back on screen as they set off, and the world scrolls crisp again
Fixed: in French the map and the saves screen ran off the right of the screen; long lines now wrap and rows of buttons flow onto a second line, and every screen is checked to fit
Fixed: menus no longer jump for a blink when they redraw
Blows land with weight: the one struck flashes pure white, an arc in your weapon's colour trails every swing, and the camera punches on crits and killing blows
Fallen foes dissolve into embers or dust instead of fading away, and foes lean back before they bite, so you see it coming
Your hero springs into a run, lands a roll with a squash and winds up each swing; the camera leans the way you're heading, and doors fade through the dark
With Reduce motion on, the camera holds still and your hero keeps its shape; flashes and dissolves still show what happened
Fireflies blink over the grass and in the woods at dusk and by night, glowing in the dark
Leaves drift down through the forests, dust floats in the light of every room, and embers rise from forges, hearths and camp fires
Your feet kick up dust on dry ground and splash through the bogs, and steel throws sparks off armour

Each region has its own air: heat shimmers over the Ash Fields as embers drift up, snow falls on the Frostgate and frost creeps in at the edges of the view, low fog rolls over the Mirefen and the marshes, and salt spray blows off the Saltmere coast
Now and then a shower crosses the open land: rain slants down and splashes, the light turns grey, the lamps come up, the birds fall quiet and you hear the rain
Each region has its own colour mood, and the night takes a little colour from everything
With Reduce motion on, nothing falls or drifts and the heat haze holds still
The wind moves the world: trees, wheat and flowers sway, their tops more than their feet, as gusts roll across the land
Water comes alive: it swells with light, glints here and there, foam laps along every shore, and what stands on a bank is mirrored in it
Cloud shadows drift slowly over the open land by day, never indoors or underground
With Reduce motion on, the wind drops and the water and the clouds hold still
Bright things now glow in the dark: lamps, fires, torches, lit windows and spells bloom softly around themselves at night and underground, while the pixels stay crisp and daylight stays clear
Glow can be turned off in Options
The world now darkens with the hour instead of under a veil: gold dawns, orange dusks and blue nights, and lamps, lit windows, torches, camp fires and hearths truly light the dark around them
Your hero carries a lantern at night and below ground, and spells light up the ground where they land
Dungeons and caves are dark and torchlit, and the Night of Ash glows red; damage numbers, prompts, health bars and danger marks stay bright in the dark
Fixed: on an AZERTY keyboard, hints named the number keys by their symbol ("Ampersand"); they read as their digits again

The Deep Hunt has named monsters of its own, posted on the board as you reach them: Grimshade, the Bone Abbot, Hollowmother and Ironheart each guard a depth's stair and leave an epic deep-forged piece
A new Feats chapter in the journal: long goals - ten and thirty depths, every bounty, every mastery, a whole set worn, the whole bestiary - each bringing home a medal for the trophy shelf
On a gamepad, A answers and confirms, X swings, B goes back everywhere, Y opens the pack, the D-pad walks, and LB, LT and RT cast your first three skills
The pad's Back button opens the dock's menu with a line chosen: every screen, and skills four to six, so a pad player can spend points and reach everything
Answers in a conversation are chosen with up and down and given with A or E, and keycaps show the pad's buttons while you play with one
Fixed: the first night's line about your skill showed a raw key token instead of its key

On a phone the controls are sized for a thumb on any screen, the attack, roll and use buttons show a drawn sword, arrow and hand instead of words, and all six skill keys are on screen, with each skill's icon
The tap bar carries what only a key did: drop, drop all and sort in the pack, put a skill on a key and forget in Skills, and it shrinks to fit the screen
A phone starts with large text, which now reaches the shops' and ledgers' descriptions too
The Deep Hunt now deepens gear for every slot, from gloves and boots to amulets and shields, the regions' sets and the named pieces
A deep piece can still be forged and masterworked: the deep's bonus is kept apart from the forge's, and pieces from before are mended once as your save loads
Tiers past Eldritch count on in numerals, and deep gear's worth grows more gently with each tier
Hilda quenches deep pieces: gold and a gem for +1 to their strongest stat, half again dearer each time
The Deep Hunt's foes now climb faster than a hero levels: the first depths are as fair as ever, but by depth thirty a mountain kit alone no longer holds
Once your whole skill tree is learned, spare skill points buy ranks beyond it in Stats: more skill power, health back from every blow, and more health, each capped
Greater potions, phoenix draughts and elixirs heal a share of your health when that's more than their own, and a new deepest depth's hoard holds a better potion the deeper you go
The rank-up says what its bonus point is truly for

releases.codename: The Deep Hunt Has a Reason
notes: The Deep Hunt has milestones at depths 5, 10, 15, 20, 30 and 50: each brings home a crystal for the trophy shelf, with stats while it's displayed, and Maren and the town hear of it
Every tenth depth a warden guards the stair down, a boss with its own attacks: the Deep Warden, then the Hollow King
Most depths now have a twist, shown at the gate: swift foes, warded skills, venomous bites or proud elites, with richer drops and a richer hoard
The gate opens the first depth of every five you've reached, so a long descent no longer starts from the top
Sounds are never quite the same twice, a little higher or lower, louder or softer; a flurry of hits sounds as one, and footsteps are softer, left foot and right
When every voice is busy, the sounds that matter (a hurt, a level, a victory) still get through
Buying, spending a stat point, a refusal, turning a dialogue's page, taking a quest and an ailment landing are all heard now, and every screen sounds as it opens and closes
Every screen keeps its title and its keys in the same places, with leaving always last as Esc close, and the keys on buttons stand on keycaps instead of being spelled out
Your gold is shown the same way everywhere: the coin and the sum
The codex's bestiary turns its pages instead of running off the screen, the pause card stays centred in French, and the phone's tap bar shows real arrows
A fall now costs at least a night at the inn, and no longer wakes the wilds: what you cleared stays cleared, and what beat you is still out there
Health comes back slowly while you're out of a fight
A delivery says how it stands as its goods come in, and when it's ready; the project board and the workbenches ask before using what a delivery you've taken still needs
The Hamlet's projects each bring something: Odo pays a tenth more, Hilda forges and Vex brews for a tenth less, and a night at the rebuilt inn leaves you well rested for a while
Townsfolk drawn from the same sheet now wear their own colours, so no two people on a map look alike
A level gained bursts in gold on the hero with LEVEL UP over their head, the experience line flashes, and the news goes on the message plate instead of slipping into the battle log
A fine or epic drop's name rises over the fallen foe in its colour
Messages wait their turn instead of cutting each other off, and stay long enough to read (longer with large text); a finished quest sounds its victory
A town's new age is heralded with a flourish and dust on the square, and each new map fades in from the dark instead of cutting (not with reduced motion)
A foe gives you longer to see its bite coming, and shows it: it crouches with a red glint and a sound. With Clear warnings on, a band on the ground marks where the bite lands
Below a quarter of your health, the health bar beats, and in a fight you hear your heart

Bosses and named monsters carry a bar across the top of the screen, notched where a boss's next phase begins. Each phase is roared, marks on the ground are heard as they appear and as they strike, and a boss falls in slow motion, with a flash and a silence before the victory sting
A critical hit shows: its number pops up in gold, twice the size, with a "!"; numbers in a flurry land side by side instead of on top of each other
A blow shoves a foe back and the push fades, instead of a one-frame jolt: an elite gives half as much ground, a boss none
The killing blow lands harder: a white flash, a longer pause and a thud; swings and skills have their own sounds. With reduced motion, no flash, pop or pause
The cutscenes' title cards and captions speak French, the doors keep their signs in French once you own a house, and switching language mid-game renames the Deep Hunt and the journal's leads at once

Small things put right: hero creation answers its keys again (role, look, the first night), the hero swings whatever weapon is in hand, Hilda's craft list moves without a stutter, and the Lich Crown's every stat includes endurance
Skill points stop lighting the menu once there's nothing left to learn
EVERY CLASS STARTS RIGHT: a new rogue carries a worn dagger that cuts with dexterity, not a strength sword - twice the bite in the first fights
A cleric's first night tells them to strike the embers down and mend between blows, since Mend is no weapon

THE TRUTH OF IT: Maren keeps the barred gate's words until it opens - no more talk of an open gate north of the bridge the morning after the fire - and says the next step in her own voice instead of telling you to ask her
The quest is now Relics of the Five - four to find, the five's to bring home - and the town's goals and the bounty board no longer offer floors behind a barred gate
In the Ashes, Hilda's and Vex's crafts are at their stalls on the square; Sela's slimes are in her stores, Wren lost her stable to the fire, and Ana warns of the packs, not the grass

THE FIRST FIELDS: a pack never hides a stronger kind than the one leading it - the slimes east of the gate come three at a time for Sela's quest, and the orc packs by the Ash road are orcs, with no wyvern among them
The wyverns keep to the far end of the Ash Fields, the journal only points at floors once the mountain's gate is open, and a scattered pack tells you when another comes
IN THEIR OWN WORDS: the villagers ask for their quests themselves again - what they need, why, and where to look - before the quest goes in your journal
The first quest you take shows where the journal is, and every accepted quest says so
Iva's marsh lies west of the gate, as it always did
KEYS THAT TELL THE TRUTH: every key the game names is the one on your keyboard - an AZERTY board reads Z, Q and W where a QWERTY one reads W, A and Z - and follows you when you rebind
Dropping a piece of gear or a whole stack asks for the same key again, and a key with a fixed job (drop, a skill, Esc) can't be given to another action
NOTHING LOST: what you buy, sell, craft or equip in a shop or your pack is saved as soon as you close it, and the game saves while any screen is open
In the browser, the game saves the moment its tab is hidden or closed, and a private window that won't keep saves says so on the title
Turning down your old web hero takes you to the title to make a new one - no more playing a stand-in that's never saved
ONE SCREEN AT A TIME: the keys go only to the screen on top. A rank-up at Morvax's fall no longer hides the throne - and the E meant for the rank-up can't choose his fate behind your back
Under the hood, a test keeps the French whole: a new line can't ship in English only
PIXELHEIM SPEAKS FRENCH: every menu, quest, line of dialogue, item, skill, monster, the story and these notes, all 3,098 strings - choose it under Options, or the game follows your system's language
Names that sit in a sentence lose their capital article in French, gear and floor foes are named in French word order, and door signs, skill icons and message tags work in either language
Every price, tag and stat abbreviation on the screens goes through the translation, so nothing is left in English in the corners

THE LAST WAGON DOWN: once his strongbox is home, Gunnar asks you to walk the pass's last wagon down from the cave mouth. Old Bergit the mammoth hauls it - slowly, and she stops dead whenever anything with teeth comes near. Three ambushes wait along the road; stay close, clear them, and keep the wagon in one piece

AGAINST THE CLOCK: Pell's canary can't breathe the shafts' bad air for long. Once she's in your pack you have a minute to get her to Pell - the clock shows top right - or she flies back to the west gallery and you fetch her again
The journal says where an escort starts

STAKES: some quests now end in a choice. In Greyhold, Fenwick's old crew still hides in the low cells - keep his secret or tell Ulla. On the Saltmere beach, Rook wants half the smugglers' captain's take - split it with him or give it back to the town. Each answer pays its own way, and the one who asked remembers
A FALL COSTS SOMETHING: waking at the inn now costs a tenth of the gold you carry. What's banked with Mirelle is safe, and the night of the fire costs nothing
A question in a conversation is answered with 1 or 2, or a click on the answer; Esc leaves it for later
ONE HERO EVERYWHERE: the save slots show each hero in what they wore, as the dock and the doll do
A necromancer's grave violet stays on their own robe and hood: borrowed iron, leather or a gilded plate keeps its colour
The fallen lie in one piece: a hero in a helmet from one set and armour from another no longer falls as two halves of two different heroes

EVERY LEAD TRUE: where a material comes from now names every way there is - patches and fights in its region, the floors' patches, chests, fishing holes (Linnea's icefin comes through the ice at the Frostgate), quest rewards, the monsters that carry it, loot and the floors' hoards - the nearest first
LOOT WHERE IT FALLS: wild loot names the regions that drop it (imp horn in the Mirefen, wolf pelts in the forest, marsh and on the coast), not a floor of the mountain
HONEST SHELVES: a shop is only named while it has the thing on its shelves, and Fafnyr's scale is sure the first time, then one in ten
MADE, NOT FOUND: the journal tells a crafting quest where it's made and what goes in

CURRENT WORDS: Loras wants his lute back from the troll and Mirelle two gems for her vault, as their quests say, not old prices; the Town age's goal says its fountain will still want Fafnyr's scale; a recipe's missing material always names itself
A quest's goods can't be sold, from any screen

PAST TEN: every skill tree grows two more tiers, at levels 13 and 17 - a new skill and two passives at each. Each role gains a skill that strikes every foe in reach (Cleave, Flame Wave, Fan of Knives, Holy Nova, Volley, Divine Storm, Death Cloud) and one more to finish (Rally, Arcane Lance, Garrote, Sunfire, Kill Shot, Shieldbreaker, and Drain Life, which heals you for half of what it takes)

PASSIVES THAT PLAY: fleeing never happened in a real-time fight, so every node and path that promised it now gives quicker feet, a dodge that's ready sooner, or a sure crit on your next strike after a dodge. New passives heal you for a share of the damage you deal, make your skills hit harder or your heals restore more
YOUR KEYS, YOUR CHOICE: in Skills, choose a skill you know and press 1-6 to put it on that key. A new skill takes the first free key, and learning one never shuffles the others
A FIFTH RANK: level 20 crowns the hero - Ironlord, Starcaller, Nightlord, Hierophant, Eldwarden, Exemplar or Deathlord - with an amethyst aura and a bonus skill point
The skill tree fits all six tiers on one page, one line a skill, with the chosen one described in full below

KILLS THAT COUNT: the Reach's chapters - the Saltmere coast and its sea cave, the mines and their shafts, Greyhold and its cellars, the Frostgate and its ice cave - pay nearly half again as much XP for a kill as the fields round Pixelheim
PUNCHING UP PAYS: a foe above your level pays 5% more XP for each level it stands above you, up to a quarter more, so a hero who has fallen behind catches up faster
Under the hood, the pacing model follows each villager's quests in the order they're offered, and every kill quest is handed in where its quarry lives

READABLE DANGER: a foe shows its level as you come near, on a small plate over its head - grey well below you, cream a match, orange a step above, red far above - so you can choose your fights before the charge

FLOORS NAME THEIR FOES: the mountain's lifted monsters wear their floor's name (a Cellar Slime, a Barrow Skeleton, an Elite Frosthowl Dire Wolf), and the Deep Hunt's are Deep ones, so a slime fifteen levels up no longer looks like the one from the forest
THE CODEX REMEMBERS: each kind you've fought is entered on its own, with the highest level you met it at and its health, attack, defence and XP there
CLEARER SKILLS: Dexterity says it strikes with bows, daggers and DEX skills, and the readout shows the attack it gives; the hero creation screen lists skills without their level

A HOME WORTH HAVING: a night in your own bed leaves you well rested (+10% XP for your next 30 fights), and furniture now helps where it stands - a bookshelf for XP, a banner for critical blows, candles for energy, a rug for gold, a plant for stronger potions, a bench for longer rest. The Manor's garden grows herbs and reeds for the cauldron

ASKED BEFORE BIG BUYS: the house deed and the workbench ask before they take your gold - press again to buy. Furniture never blocks the doorway, an upgrade hands back what stood in its way, and new hints explain the house, deeds and the bank

LATE GOLD, TAMED: past the mountain, the Deep Hunt's foes pay a little more each depth rather than ever more steeply, and a depth you've already cleared pays its foes a quarter. The dead Morvax raises pay nothing, and Fafnyr's scale is sure the first time you bring him down, then rare

GOLD WITH A PURPOSE: from Smithing 8 Hilda forges past the cap, up to +12, each step dearer than the last and a gem a time; once Pixelheim is a city its shops sell the King's Signet, the Aegis of the Ash and the Everflask; and when every age is built the town takes commissions - the Statue of the Five (+5% XP), the Lantern Walk (+10% gold) and the Healers' Hall (potions heal a quarter more)

PROPERTY THAT PAYS: a business you own now fills its till with rent every day - about a twenty-fifth of what its deed cost, a tenth more once Pixelheim is a village and a quarter more expanded - and its keeper hands you the till when you walk up to the counter. No more rent line after every kill
AN OWNER'S PERKS: you pay a tenth less in a shop you own, and its shelf keeps an owner's pick that changes every day
HOLDINGS: the town hall's page now lists what you own - what each property has earned, what waits in its till and what a day brings

AN HONEST BANK: Mirelle's savings now pay half a percent a day on what's in the pot, up to a tenth of it in all, and the interest is kept apart - topping up no longer folds it in or restarts the clock, so a pot can't be grown without end. The bank shows what your savings have earned so far, and there's a Deposit all
THE BANK COMES SOONER: Mirelle settles once Pixelheim is a village, so her bank opens while you're still out in the regions

MASTERY SHOWS IN THE WORK: the further your trade stands above a recipe, the likelier what you forge or weave comes out Fine - and, well past it, Epic, with the bonus stats loot has. Your own workbench at home counts as a level more

OLD GEAR BACK TO THE FORGE: Hilda's new Salvage tab breaks a piece down into half of what it was made of (or ember shards), and from Smithing 8 her Reforge tab rolls a piece's rarity again - never down - with fresh bonus stats
CRAFTING QUESTS: Brin wants an oilskin coat for the harbour, Garrick a helm forged from his Blackiron seam, and Linnea a Frostweave hood for her brother on the pass

EVERY RECIPE WORTH MAKING: no early recipe waits on a late monster (the Beast Cleaver and the smith's gauntlets take ember shards now, not imp horns), and nothing costs more to make than it's worth. The dragon recipes are real endgame gear - Scaled Mail at 12 armour, a Grave Ward at 8, a Wyrmfang Dagger at 20 - and a Dragon Tonic brings everything back

TRADES THAT KEEP UP: a craft teaches more the harder the recipe, the Frostweave can be woven from Alchemy 2, and Vex's cauldron lets you steep two bought potions into one better one for the practice. Smithing 9 forges one step higher and Smithing 10 forges every piece Fine

SMALL FIXES: the starter buckler no longer out-guards the coast's, the floor-7 hoard stops giving away what the forge makes, hunter's stew is made from fish, and pearls bite more often at the Saltmere jetty

A LOOT CURVE WORTH CHASING: the mountain's floors drop by how deep they are, so every band of floors is a step up - the Obsidian Blade waits on the last floors, and Dragonbane's hoard (now 23 damage) is no longer a step down. Gear drops more often, and a boss always drops a piece

NEW TO FIND: the Starfall Staff, the Gale Longbow and the Moonsteel Dagger on the deep floors, so mages, rangers and rogues have something to chase as well. In the Deep Hunt, gear comes up forged deeper every five depths: Deep-forged, Abyssal, Primordial
MIXED PACKS: a pack in the wilds is no longer three of a kind - its leader brings company from the region, though never anything much stronger than itself

LOOT THAT FITS THE STAGE: a monster in the wilds drops what a monster of its level would, never more than its region's best - the Mirefen's skeletons no longer drop the mountain's finest blades, and the maze chest there holds a steel axe instead of an obsidian blade

ARMOUR SETS, READ RIGHT: a set's line now shows what each tier adds up to (five pieces of Oilskin give +5 DEX, not +3), the Greyhold Warden set guards a little better than the Blackiron that comes before it, and the shop says which stat a weapon hits with

READY FOR OTHER LANGUAGES: every word the game shows - its menus, messages, quests, dialogue, items and story - can now be translated, and Options has a Language row (it follows your system's language unless you pick one). French is on its way

A FIRST NIGHT YOU CAN SKIP: hero creation has a First night toggle (Tab) for players who have walked it before

A DAWN YOU WATCH: when Maren has the letter, the Night of Ash ends on the town itself. THE AGES BUILD ON PLANNED LOTS: new cottages rise by the river walk, the barn across the bridge, lamps along Upper Street and then the gate road, and the fountain at the square's heart. A walled garden hides between the homes and the river - and someone left something in it

ONE PLATE FOR WHAT THE GAME TELLS YOU: the next step, a message and every line of the battle log now sit on the same dark plate, readable over grass and snow alike, with a gold word in front where it helps (Next, Quest accepted, Quest complete, Level up, Mastery)

KEYS THAT LOOK LIKE KEYS: every key the game shows you - in a screen's footer, under a conversation, in the menu - is drawn as a raised key with a lit edge and a lip, and it dips when you press it. Pairs sit side by side (W S), choices take a slash (I / Esc), and the arrow keys show their arrows

MATCHING SUMMONS AND POISONS: the dead Morvax raises stand at his level, and monsters on the mountain's floors poison and burn as hard as their level, not their kind's

A SAFER MIREFEN AND DEEPWOOD: the Mirefen's mimic pack is gone (its trapped chest waits in the far west, by Grandmother Gulp), and the Deepwood's trolls no longer stand at its gate

SHOPS FOLLOW THE STORY: Hilda's, Vex's and Odo's shelves now fill as you win the relics out in the Reach, not only as you climb the mountain - iron, staves and leather from the start, steel and better rings with each relic
MANA AND CURES FROM DAY ONE: Vex sells mana potions and antidotes from the first morning, and Odo dried meat

A TRADER IN EVERY REGION: Marta the Chandler in Saltmere, Quartermaster Brann at the Blackiron camp, Mabel the Sutler by Greyhold's road, and Gunnar's caravan on the Frostgate pass - each with their own pack and one rare piece

GLOVES, BOOTS AND SHIELDS SHOW: gauntlets colour your hands, boots your feet, and the shield you carry hangs on your off hand - a round buckler, a kite or a tower, in its own colours, in front of you or behind as you turn, put away while you draw a bow or cast

EVERY SET FROM HEAD TO TOE: Saltmere's oilskin with its saltwood buckler, Blackiron's soot plate and black bulwark, the Warden's slate and kite, Frostweave's white with the rime orb glowing at your side
The paper doll and the dock's portrait wear it all too

EVERY HELM AND BODY HAS A LOOK OF ITS OWN: Saltmere's oilskin is tarred sea-green, Blackiron soot-black with ember-hot horns, the Warden Greyhold slate with a cyan plume, Frostweave ice white, the City Plate gold on royal blue, Scaled Mail copper on dragon green, Greymaw's Hood wolf grey - and the cloaks, robes and iron each their own

Paladins in soldier's steel, the mayor, Hilda, Odo, Sela and the goblins and orcs no longer step one frame out of time: their swings, stumbles and falls play the frames they were drawn for

THE WEAPON YOU HOLD IS THE WEAPON YOU SWING: a warrior who picks up a bow draws it, a mage with a war hammer swings it, and a ranger with a staff casts. Bare-handed, every hero keeps their own way of fighting

BLADES IN THEIR OWN COLOURS: Dragonbane swings red, the Obsidian Blade violet, the Blackiron Axe soot-dark, the Warden's Longsword Greyhold steel, Tidecutter sea-green - and bows and staves take their wood and stone too

ANY WAY UP: the game fills a phone's screen held sideways or upright instead of sitting in a letterbox, the dock along the bottom and the pages in the middle. Upright, the art stays big enough to see the hero; sideways reads best, and the game says so once
On a computer nothing changes

THE TOWN SENDS YOU OUT: once Maren has asked for the relics, Pixelheim's folk have errands in the Reach - Hilda wants Blackiron ore, Vex wants Saltmere's sea glass, Sela has heard of the smugglers' rum, Bram needs the miners' humming cheese, Ana her father's badge from Greyhold and Mira yeti fur from the Frostgate. SIDE QUESTS FOLLOW THE STORY: a hub's side quests wait for its first word - Rook after Wenna's smugglers, Pell after the lost crew, Fenwick once the yard is clear, Gunnar once the wolves are gone

THE MAP MARKS WHO IS WAITING: villagers with a quest to give or take back show as green squares on the map

THE STORY IN CHAPTERS: Out of the Ashes, The Five Relics, The Ashen Throne, The Deathless. The line above the dock points at the next relic still out there
MAREN REMEMBERS: each relic you win brings her story of its owner - Tam's stew in the snow, the five marks on the black iron, Oskar's shield and Liane's lantern

THE REACH GROWS THE TOWN: two relics open the Village age and all four the Town, and the bounty board posts its notices as relics are won
The region chapters' quests and bosses pay half the XP they did, so a hero arrives at each one about its match
Long messages now grow upward instead of running under the dock
A hero from before keeps everything: whoever has cleared a floor finds the gate open, and Maren goes straight to her next ask

THE HERMIT AND THE CARAVAN: Aske keeps Liane's door fifty years on; Gunnar's caravan is stuck by the road, and Linnea, its herbalist, picks frost lilies for Vex

THE ICE CAVE: down the observatory's stair, yetis, wendigos and frost mammoths in frosted galleries - and Rimefang, a white drake that breathes frost, curled up on Liane's Lantern, the fourth of the five relics
ICE FISHING: stand at the hole cut in the lake's ice, face the water and press E for icefin
THE FROSTWEAVE: hood, robe, mitts, boots and a rime orb (+INT), and the Rime Staff - woven at Vex's cauldron from frost lilies and yeti fur

GREYHOLD: a new road leaves the east edge of the Ash Fields for Oskar's old fort on its hill - breached walls, a stone yard, his statue, and the keep where turncoats in red cloaks have made themselves at home
THE OLD GUARD'S CAMP: Sergeant Ulla, Brother Teo and Fenwick, a turncoat who changed his mind, keep a guardhouse by the road with five quests between them

THE CELLARS: down the keep's stair to the guardroom, the old cells, the crypt and the captain's hall, where Greyhold's dead garrison still stands watch - and the Hollow Captain keeps Oskar's Shield, the third of the five relics
THE GREYHOLD WARDEN: helm, hauberk, gauntlets, boots and a kite shield (+STR and +DEX), and the Warden's Longsword - forged at Hilda's from the fort's old steel
THE BLACKIRON MINES: a new road leaves the west edge of the Ash Fields into a valley of spoil and scrub, with a miners' camp on the road and the shaft mouth in the northern cliff

THE SHAFTS: torchlit galleries of goblin diggers and spearmen, stone golems in the cart hall, ore veins in the dead ends - and the Seam Warden, an iron demon guarding the deep seam. It leaves the Black Ingot, the second of the five relics
MINERS' QUESTS: Foreman Garrick's lost crew and the black seam, Dagny's ore and cart hall, and Old Pell's canary, lost somewhere off the west gallery
THE BLACKIRON PLATE: helm, plate, gauntlets, sabatons and a bulwark (+STR, heavy), and the Blackiron Axe - forged at Hilda's from the seam's ore
The release flows give the camera-smoothness check a second try, so a busy machine no longer fails it
ARMOUR SETS: pieces of one set worn together give more - at three pieces and again at five. The bonus shows on every piece (what you wear of it, what more would give) and on the stats page

THE SALTMERE OILSKIN: hood, coat, gloves, boots and a saltwood buckler, light and quick (+DEX), and the Tidecutter, a sea-glass dagger on a pearl grip. Hilda crafts them from what the coast gives: sea glass, pelts, fish and pearls
Every region still to come brings its own set
The craft guide now knows fishing: it tells you where the fish and pearls a recipe needs come from
SALTMERE'S PEOPLE: Old Wenna, whose brother Tam climbed the mountain fifty years ago and never came back; Harbourmaster Brin; Ola the Fisher; and Rook, the honest kind of smuggler

THE SEA CAVE under the western headland: six torchlit chambers of drowned skeletons, slimes and crabs, two chests - and the Tidecaller in its grotto. It leaves Tam's Ladle, the first of the five relics

QUESTS on the coast: the smugglers' story and the Tidecaller for Wenna, crabs on the jetty and the lighthouse lens for Brin, your first catch for Ola, the smugglers' captain for Rook - and in Pixelheim, Pip's cat wants fresh fish
FISHING: stand at the end of Saltmere's jetty, by the lagoon or on the eastern rocks, face the water and press E. Fish, sea glass, the odd pearl - and the odd boot
NEW FOES from Shade's Mini World: giant crabs, smugglers, gunners, their captain and the slime king

THE REACH GROWS: a new road leaves the bottom of the marsh, down through the cliffs to SALTMERE - dunes and pines, a fishing hamlet on the beach, a lagoon, a jetty out into the sea and a cave under the western headland
THE COAST is wild: slimes, goblin smugglers and drowned skeletons keep their camps on its dunes and beaches, and sea glass washes up to gather - a new crafting material
Saltmere's doors are shut for now: its people, their quests and the sea cave come with the coast's own chapter
Behind the scenes: new ground for the regions to come (Shade's sea in three depths, docks, snow, ice and cobbled stone) and a tool that turns a drawn sketch into a map

LARGE READING TEXT: everything you read at length - conversations, the story's captions, the town tour, hints, the quest line, the battle log and messages - in the big type. Long lines grow the window upward instead of running off the screen

HINTS: the first time something hunts you, the game tells you about the dodge roll (with your own key); each new skill says what it does when you learn it; the notice board and the bounty board explain themselves the first time you walk up. Once each, and Hints in Options turns them off
Story captions now wrap instead of running past the edge of the screen

DUSK ON THE SQUARE: as the sun goes down the townsfolk walk to the square and stand about the well, then go home for the night

SHOPS GROW WITH THE TOWN: each new age brings Odo, Hilda and Vex more stock, and a signature item you can only buy in Pixelheim - Lamplighter's Sausages and the Lamplit Blade in the Village, a Fountain Day Roast, the Fountain Guard and a Fountain Tonic in the Town, Banquet Ribs, City Plate and a Phoenix Draught in the City

STORY THEMES: Fafnyr and Morvax each have a theme of their own as they first appear, the dawn after the Night of Ash has one, and each ending has its own before the victory music takes over
